The contract method is `public function ask(string $prompt, array $history = [], ?string $scope = null): string` (App\Contracts\AiProvider:51), and all three concrete drivers already accept `$history`, pass it through `AbstractAiProvider::sanitiseHistory()`, and emit an ARRAY OF TURNS on the wire: OpenAiProvider sends `messages` = [system] + alternating user/assistant turns + current user prompt; AnthropicProvider sends top-level `system` plus a `messages` array of user/assistant turns + current prompt; GeminiProvider sends a `contents` array of `{role: user|model, parts:[{text}]}` turns, with the system prompt GLUED onto the final user turn (`systemContext($scope)."\n\nUser question: ".$prompt`) rather than sent as `system_instruction`. Only NullAiProvider ignores history (documented: "ignored — nothing is sent anywhere"). AiController::query() reads the prior turns via transcript() BEFORE inserting the new question, then calls `$this->ai->ask($prompt, $history, $this->policy->scopeFor($user))`. Storage roles are 'user'|'ai'; each driver maps 'ai' → 'assistant' (OpenAI/Anthropic) or 'model' (Gemini). sanitiseHistory() drops synthetic replies (a leading '⚠️' or AiAccessPolicy::REFUSAL_PREFIX) together with the question they answered, forces strict user→ai alternation by popping the OLDER duplicate, drops a trailing unanswered user turn, then caps by turn count (`history_turns`, default 20) and total characters (`history_chars`, default 12000) from the oldest end, finally re-dropping any leading 'ai' turn so Anthropic's "must start on user" rule holds. Model selection: `models()` = configured model first, then `fallback_models` from config, uniqued/filtered; each driver loops `foreach ($this->models() as $model)` and `continue`s to the next on 404 (OpenAI also on 400/404 when `looksLikeModelError()`), returning a "⚠️ Unable to reach … with the configured models." string if the loop exhausts. Only `gemini` and `anthropic` define `fallback_models` in config/services.php; `openai` and `compatible` have no such key, so `models()` returns a single element there. Failure convention is uniform: never throw, always return a string beginning with '⚠️' (`missingKey()`, "⚠️ {label} API Error ({status}): {msg}", "⚠️ AI service error: {message}"). AiController is 522 lines, 18 methods (8 public routed + 10 private), 12 DB::table() call sites across ai_chat_sessions and ai_chat_messages, both PHP-UUID-keyed with hand-set timestamps per the project's Query Builder style.

findings.what: The entire contract: ONE method. History is already a first-class parameter, defaulting to [] so one-shot callers (CompetencyGapAnalysisService) are unaffected. The docblock fixes the storage shape as ['role' => 'user'|'ai', 'message' => string], oldest first, and states drivers must not trust the list. Also documents the STATELESSNESS reason history is passed per call: drivers are memoised singletons shared by every consumer.

Constants and constructor DI. HISTORY_LIMIT caps transcript() reads; ACTION_VERBS is the pre-filter that decides whether the planner runs at all; CONFIRM_TTL_MINUTES bounds a parked destructive action.
sessions(Request $request) — no validation. Returns JSON {"sessions": [...]}, each row {id,title,created_at,updated_at}, most-recently-updated first, hard limit 100.

storeSession(Request $request) — no validation; delegates to createSession(auth()->id()) and returns {"session": {id,title:null,created_at,updated_at}} with HTTP 201. sessionMessages(Request $request, string $session) — no validation; ownedSession() 404-gates, returns {"session": {...}, "messages": [...]}.

updateSession(Request $request, string $session) — validates ['title' => 'required|string|max:120'], updates title (trimmed) + updated_at, returns {"ok":true,"title":"..."}. destroySession(Request $request, string $session) — no validation; one transaction deleting ai_chat_messages by (user_id, session_id) then ai_chat_sessions by (id, user_id), because session_id has no FK/cascade. Returns {"ok":true}.

history(Request $request) — no validation. Selects only ['id','title'] of the newest session by updated_at, returns {"session": {id,title}|null, "messages": [...]|[]}. This is the sidebar's no-session-selected fallback.

query(Request $request) — validation rules are exactly query: required|string|max:1000 and session_id: nullable|string|max:36. THIS IS THE HISTORY CALL SITE: transcript() is read BEFORE the new question is inserted so the prompt is not duplicated in the replay, and the third argument is the per-request RBAC scope string. seq is derived as (int) max('seq') + 1 per insert. Message insert columns: id (Str::uuid()), user_id, session_id, role, message, seq, created_at, updated_at.

query()'s tail: the 'ai' row is inserted with the same column set and a fresh now() (deliberately not the question's timestamp), the session title is derived from the first prompt if still null and updated_at bumped, then the exact JSON shape returned for XHR/JSON requests — four keys plus response. Non-AJAX POST falls back to back()->with('ai_response', $response).

clearHistory(Request $request) — NO validate() call; session_id is taken straight off $request->input('session_id') and, when present, routed through destroySession() (which re-reads it via ownedSession() and 404s, so the ownership check still holds). Without one, both tables are wiped for the user inside a transaction. Returns {"ok":true} in both branches.

private resolveAction(Request $request, object $session, $user, string $prompt): ?array — returns null to mean "answer conversationally" (which is what lets the ask() history call happen). Order: pending confirmation first (cleared, then a confirm-regex decides execute vs 'Cancelled — nothing was changed.'), then the ACTION_VERBS pre-filter, then planner->plan(), then a 'missing' report, then AiActionRegistry::get($plan['action'], $user) for the role check, then destructive prepare+park, else executor->execute(). $plan is stamped with the raw prompt and session_id before registry lookup.

private reply(string $message, ?string $status, bool $pending = false): array — the {message,status,pending} envelope. private pendingAction(object $session): ?array reads first(['pending_action','pending_action_at']) and expires past CONFIRM_TTL_MINUTES via now()->diffInMinutes($row->pending_action_at, true). private storePending(object,array): void writes pending_action (json_encode), pending_action_at, updated_at. private clearPending(object): void nulls pending_action + pending_action_at (and deliberately does NOT touch updated_at). private listWords(array): string builds "the a, b and c".

The three private internals that matter for history. ownedSession() is the whole access control (user_id predicate + abort_if 404, never 403). createSession(int $userId) inserts id/user_id/title=null/created_at/updated_at and returns a plain object without user_id. transcript(string $sessionId) is the exact history source: filtered by BOTH user_id and session_id, ordered by seq DESC then created_at DESC, limited to 200 (newest end), then reversed to oldest-first; selects exactly ['role','message','created_at'] and maps to arrays with those same three keys — so 'created_at' rides along into the array that ask() receives, and sanitiseHistory() simply ignores it.

The failure-return convention in code: missingKey() is the '⚠️'-prefixed no-key string every driver returns before making any HTTP call. Combined with each driver's "⚠️ {label} API Error ({status}): {msg}", '⚠️ AI service error: '.$e->getMessage(), and the exhausted-models string, this is the complete failure vocabulary — nothing throws. decodeJson() closes the loop by treating a leading '⚠️' as null.

OpenAI/compatible request body — verbatim. SENDS AN ARRAY OF TURNS, not a single user string: 'messages' is buildMessages() output = one system message, then every sanitised turn mapped 'ai'->'assistant', then the current prompt as the final user message. Endpoint POST {base}/chat/completions with withToken() Bearer auth; response read from 'choices.0.message.content'. Model loop continues on 400/404 when looksLikeModelError() matches 'model' in the message or code in ['model_not_found','invalid_model'].

Anthropic request body — verbatim. SENDS AN ARRAY OF TURNS: 'messages' = sanitised turns ('ai'->'assistant') + current prompt; the system prompt is the separate top-level 'system' field, so buildMessages() takes NO $scope argument (scope reaches the wire only via systemContext($scope) at the call site, line 44). Headers x-api-key + anthropic-version (config 'anthropic_version', default '2023-06-01'). Reply read from 'content.0.text'. Model loop continues only on 404.

Gemini request body — verbatim. SENDS AN ARRAY OF TURNS in 'contents', roles 'user'/'model'. The one structural difference from the other two: there is NO system field — systemContext($scope) is concatenated onto the final user turn with "\n\nUser question: " because system_instruction is unsupported on older models. Endpoint POST {base}/models/{model}:generateContent?key={apiKey} (key in the query string, no header). Reply read from 'candidates.0.content.parts.0.text'. Model loop continues only on 404.

The ONLY driver that does not accept history in any meaningful sense — it implements AiProvider directly (does not extend AbstractAiProvider) and its docblock says the parameter is ignored. Returns a '⚠️'-prefixed config-diagnostic string naming the bad AI_PROVIDER value and the configured alternatives.

findings.verbatim:
WHY session_id carries NO foreign key: adding an FK through Schema::table()
 * makes Laravel's SQLite grammar rebuild the whole table (copy to __temp__,
 * drop, rename). That rebuild reconstructs columns from BlueprintState, which
 * does not capture CHECK constraints — so the role enum('user','ai'), which
 * SQLite implements as `varchar check (role in (...))`, would be silently
 * downgraded to a plain varchar in the test database while MySQL keeps a real
 * ENUM. The same rebuild also copies rows with `pragma foreign_keys` off, so an
 * FK that MySQL would reject on existing history passes green in CI. Ownership
 * is instead enforced in AiController, which scopes every session read/write by
 * auth()->id(); deleting a session explicitly deletes its messages first.
findings.what: Documented reason session_id has no FK — this is the constraint the route-file comment at line 355-356 refers to. Ownership is enforced in AiController via auth()->id(), and session deletion deletes its messages first.
seq semantics: nullable because legacy adopted rows have none; readers fall back to created_at when seq is null.

risks.lens: CSS/layout collisions: a NEW permanently-dockable right sidebar (VSCode style) that PUSHES main content when open. What breaks? Think: hard-coded margins/widths, z-index stacking against existing dropdowns/modals, mobile breakpoints, horizontal scrollbars, the existing left sidebar collapse logic, tables that already overflow.

risks.title: A pushing right sidebar already exists — a second one collides for the same viewport column and the same single offset variable
risks.detail: `#ai-rail` (partials/ai-rail.blade.php:17, hims.css:987-1011) is already a VSCode-style dockable right sidebar: `position: fixed; top:0; right:0; bottom:0; width: var(--hims-ai-w); z-index: 98`, off-canvas via `transform: translateX(100%)` + `visibility: hidden`, drag-resizable, with open/width/session persisted in localStorage (hims.blade.php:620-668). The push mechanism is ONE custom property with exactly two consumers in the whole stylesheet: `--hims-ai-offset`, read at hims.css:175 (`.hims-topbar { right: }`) and hims.css:501 (`.hims-main { margin-right: }`). There is no wrapper element, no flex/grid shell — `<body>` holds four independently-positioned siblings (hims.blade.php:31, 119, 122, 244). hims.blade.php:660-661 writes `--hims-ai-offset: var(--hims-ai-w)` as a variable *alias*, not a resolved px value. A new sidebar that writes `--hims-ai-offset` destroys that aliasing and the resize handle stops reflowing the page; a new sidebar that does NOT write it sits on top of content with no reflow at all. Making both coexist requires rewriting hims.css:175 and 501 to `calc(var(--hims-ai-offset) + var(--hims-new-offset))` — a two-line change in a hand-authored, non-cache-busted-by-filename stylesheet.

risks.title: Every modal ignores the sidebar offset and paints over the sidebar — two modals are wider than the remaining content column
risks.detail: `.hims-modal-backdrop` is `position: fixed; inset: 0; z-index: 1200` (hims.css:1335-1344) with `.open { display: flex; justify-content: center }` and `.hims-modal { margin: auto }` (1350-1361). `inset: 0` is viewport-relative and reads no offset variable, so a modal always centres on the FULL viewport, never on the narrowed content column, and z-index 1200 puts it over the rail (98). Concrete: `learning/assignments/_roster-modals.blade.php:5` overrides to `max-width:980px` and `training/sessions/_create-modal.blade.php:19` to `max-width:760px`. On a 1440px viewport with the rail dragged to its `MAX_W = 620` (hims.blade.php:627), the content column is 260-820px = 560px wide, but the 980px roster modal centres at x=720 and spans 230-1210px — covering the left sidebar edge and 390px of the right sidebar. At the 1100px push threshold the 620px content column is 220px and the modal covers it entirely plus both rails. 20+ modal partials go through this one backdrop rule.

risks.title: `body.ai-rail-docked .hims-card .card-body { overflow-x: auto }` is the ONLY desktop horizontal-scroll escape hatch, and it is class-gated on the existing rail
risks.detail: `.hims-card` is `overflow: hidden` (hims.css:551-558) and `.hims-table th` is `white-space: nowrap` (hims.css:597), so a table whose headers cannot shrink is silently CLIPPED — no scrollbar — when the column narrows. `.hims-table` has no desktop `min-width`; `min-width: 520px` exists only inside `@media (max-width: 768px)` (hims.css:1293). The single desktop rescue is hims.css:1260, keyed on the `ai-rail-docked` body class that only `applyOffset()` sets (hims.blade.php:663). `.table-responsive` is declared at hims.css:912 but used in ZERO views (grep across resources/views returns nothing), so it provides no fallback. 35 view files contain `.hims-table`. A new sidebar that pushes without toggling that exact class (or adding its own rule) clips wide tables across the app with no scrollbar and no visual cue.

risks.title: The push/overlay breakpoint is duplicated as two numbers measured off different quantities, so there is a ~15px band where JS and CSS disagree
risks.detail: JS: `const RAIL_PUSH_MIN = 1100; // keep in step with hims.css` (hims.blade.php:626) and `railOverlays() { return window.innerWidth < RAIL_PUSH_MIN }` (hims.blade.php:648). CSS: `@media (max-width: 1099px)` (hims.css:1243). `window.innerWidth` INCLUDES the classic vertical scrollbar; a `max-width` media query evaluates against the initial containing block, which EXCLUDES it. HIMS pages routinely have a vertical scrollbar (long tables, `min-height: calc(100vh - var(--hims-topbar-h))` at hims.css:503). At an outer width of ~1110px with a 15px scrollbar, `railOverlays()` returns false so JS sets `--hims-ai-offset: var(--hims-ai-w)` and hides the backdrop, while CSS simultaneously applies overlay mode: `#ai-rail { top: var(--hims-topbar-h); z-index: 100 }` and `#ai-rail-resizer { display: none }` (hims.css:1245-1251). Result in that band: the page gives up 340-620px AND the rail is pushed 64px down with its drag handle gone. Adding a second dockable sidebar with its own breakpoint pair doubles this desync surface.

risks.title: Sidebar width is clamped only to a constant, never to the viewport, and is restored from localStorage on every page load with no viewport check
risks.detail: `applyWidth(px)` clamps to `Math.min(MAX_W, Math.max(MIN_W, ...))` with `MIN_W = 280, MAX_W = 620` (hims.blade.php:627, 652) — no term involving `window.innerWidth`. `const savedWidth = parseInt(localStorage.getItem(WIDTH_KEY)...); if (savedWidth) applyWidth(savedWidth);` (hims.blade.php:667-668) replays the stored width unconditionally on every navigation. A user who drags to 620 on a 2560px monitor then opens the same account on a 1100px laptop (push mode, since `railOverlays()` is `< 1100`) gets a content column of 1100 − 260 (`--hims-sidebar-w`) − 620 = 220px, minus 56px of `.hims-main` padding (hims.css:502) = 164px usable. Combined with `.hims-table th { white-space: nowrap }` and 5-column tables, every table page is unusable. A second sidebar with its own independent MAX_W makes the worst case additive.

risks.title: The overlay backdrop sits below the topbar and the left sidebar, so both stay interactive behind the "modal" rail between 769-1099px
risks.detail: `#ai-rail-backdrop` is `z-index: 97` (hims.css:1236-1242). `.hims-topbar` is 99 (hims.css:183) and `.hims-sidebar` is 100 (hims.css:58). `.hims-sidebar` only goes off-canvas at `@media (max-width: 768px)` (hims.css:1269-1272), so in the 769-1099px band the left sidebar is fully visible and the backdrop does not cover it or the topbar — a user can navigate away while the rail is supposedly modal. Inside the same query the rail is promoted to `z-index: 100` (hims.css:1248), which TIES `.hims-sidebar`'s 100; the rail only wins because its include is at hims.blade.php:282 versus the sidebar at :31, i.e. paint order depends on DOM order, not the declared ladder. A second overlay sidebar inserted anywhere else in `<body>` inherits that fragile tie.

risks.title: Topbar dropdowns are fixed-pixel-width and clamped against `100vw`, not against the shrinking topbar they are anchored to
risks.detail: `.search-dropdown { width: 520px }` (hims.css:366) and `.notif-dropdown { width: 390px }` (hims.css:301) are anchored `position: absolute; right: 0` inside `.topbar-menu-wrap` (hims.css:245-249) with `max-width: calc(100vw - 32px)` (hims.css:252). The topbar's own width is `100vw − var(--hims-sidebar-w) − var(--hims-ai-offset)` (hims.css:174-175), but the clamp is written against `100vw`, so it never fires. On 1366px with a 620px rail docked the topbar is 486px wide — the 520px search panel overhangs its left edge and, at `z-index: 1100`, paints over the left sidebar. At the 1100px push threshold the topbar is 220px and both the 520px and the 390px panels overflow it by 300px and 170px. A second sidebar deepens the shrink; the fix is a container-relative clamp, which `calc(100vw - ...)` cannot express here.

risks.title: Only `margin-right`/`right` are transitioned — a left-sidebar collapse (which does not exist yet) would tear against the sidebar's own `all .18s`
risks.detail: There is NO desktop left-sidebar collapse in this codebase: grep for `collapsed` in hims.css and hims.blade.php returns nothing, and `--hims-sidebar-w` is only ever *read* (hims.css:53, 174, 499) — never reassigned. If the plan adds one: `.hims-main` transitions ONLY `margin-right .18s` (hims.css:504) and `.hims-topbar` only `right .18s` (hims.css:185), so `margin-left`/`left` would snap instantly while `.hims-sidebar { transition: var(--hims-transition) }` = `all .18s` (hims.css:60) animates its width — a visible 180ms tear on every collapse. The mobile path avoids this only because it swaps to `translateX(-100%)` plus `margin-left: 0` behind a media query (hims.css:1269-1281).

risks.title: `body.ai-resizing` transition suppression names exactly three selectors by hand
risks.detail: `body.ai-resizing .hims-main, body.ai-resizing .hims-topbar, body.ai-resizing #ai-rail { transition: none }` (hims.css:508-510), set/cleared by the pointerdown/pointerup handlers at hims.blade.php:718-730. Any new panel added to the shell is not in that list, so it will animate its `.18s` reflow on every `pointermove` and visibly lag the cursor — the exact failure the comment at hims.css:506-507 says the rule exists to prevent. A new sidebar with its own resizer must also add itself here.

risks.title: `departments/index.blade.php` hand-rolls a `position: fixed` modal inside the transformed `.animate-in` wrapper — it inherits the sidebar's narrowed column
risks.detail: `<div id="addDeptModal" style="display:none;position:fixed;inset:0;...z-index:999;...">` at departments/index.blade.php:109, opened/closed by inline `onclick` at :13 and :130. It is NOT in `@push('modals')`, so it renders inside `<main>` inside `<div class="animate-in">` (hims.blade.php:264-266), whose `fadeInUp` keyframes end on `transform: translateY(0)` held by `animation-fill-mode: forwards` (hims.css:1306-1313). That transform makes `.animate-in` the containing block for `position: fixed` descendants, so `inset: 0` resolves to the padding box of `.hims-main` — which carries `margin-right: var(--hims-ai-offset)` (hims.css:501). With a sidebar docked, this modal is confined to the narrowed column, and its `max-width:480px` panel (:110) cannot fit the 220px column at the push threshold. Its `z-index: 999` is also below `.topbar-dropdown` (1100), so a notification panel paints over it.

risks.title: Nothing in the stylesheet guards against horizontal document overflow
risks.detail: There is no `overflow-x: hidden` (or any `overflow` declaration) on `html` or `body` anywhere in hims.css — grep for `overflow` returns only element-level rules at 261, 350, 444, 523, 557, 678, 753, 912, 1048, 1119, 1260, 1292, 1463. `body` (hims.css:41-47) sets only font/background/margin/min-height. The existing rail depends on `visibility: hidden` rather than the transform alone precisely because of this, per the comment at hims.css:999-1002 ("a transform alone would leave a horizontal scrollbar on the body"). A new sidebar that ships closed with `transform: translateX(100%)` and no `visibility: hidden`/zero width will put a horizontal scrollbar on every one of the 46 views that `@extends('layouts.hims')`, with no page-level clamp to catch it. Note also `#ai-rail { max-width: 100vw }` (hims.css:993) and `@media (max-width:480px) { #ai-rail { width: 100vw } }` (hims.css:1253-1255) — `100vw` includes the scrollbar gutter, so the phone-width rule is already slightly over-wide.

risks.title: Two unrelated document-level Escape handlers and a body-scroll lock cross over the sidebar
risks.detail: The layout registers `document.addEventListener('keydown', ...)` closing sidebar + dropdowns + rail-if-overlaying (hims.blade.php:563-573), and `partials/modal-js.blade.php` registers a second document-level Escape handler that closes the open modal — pushed to `@stack('scripts')` at hims.blade.php:1005, so it runs after. Neither calls `stopPropagation`, so one Escape press while a modal is open in overlay mode closes the modal AND the sidebar AND the mobile drawer. Separately, `modal-js` sets `document.body.style.overflow = 'hidden'` on open and `''` on close (modal-js.blade.php:31, 39) — an unconditional write, so if a new sidebar also locks body scroll (the usual pattern for overlay mode) whichever closes last unlocks it, and the other's lock is silently released.

risks.lens: Data-layer risks: adding an ai_chat_sessions table and a session_id FK on ai_chat_messages. Existing rows have no session. What breaks on migrate? Remember this app uses raw Query Builder, CHAR(36) UUID PKs generated in PHP, manual created_at/updated_at, and phpunit runs on sqlite :memory: while prod is MySQL.

risks.title: The planned migration is a duplicate — `php artisan migrate` aborts before it runs
risks.detail: `ai_chat_sessions` already exists: `Schema::create('ai_chat_sessions', ...)` at 2026_08_06_000120_create_ai_chat_sessions_table.php:38 (id uuid PK, user_id + FK users.id cascade, title string(120) nullable, timestamps, index ['user_id','updated_at']). `ai_chat_messages.session_id` char(36) nullable already exists at the same file:53, with `seq` at :54 and index `ai_chat_messages_session_seq_index` at :56. 2026_08_07_000140_add_pending_action_to_ai_chat_sessions.php:24-26 adds pending_action/pending_action_at. A second `Schema::create('ai_chat_sessions')` throws "table already exists" (MySQL 1050 / SQLite), and a second `char('session_id', 36)` throws duplicate-column. Because migrate has no per-migration rollback here, `php artisan migrate:fresh --seed` — the documented dev reset — stops mid-run leaving a half-built schema on hims_v2. There is no `Schema::hasTable()`/`hasColumn()` guard convention anywhere in database/migrations to soften this. The correct move is to write NO new table migration: the sessions layer is already wired end to end (AiController.php:73-151 sessions/store/messages/update/destroy, routes/web.php:359-366).

risks.title: Adding the session_id FK silently strips the `role` enum CHECK from the sqlite test schema
risks.detail: Empirically confirmed on this checkout (Laravel 13.22.0): on SQLite `compileForeign()` is a deliberate no-op (vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Database/Schema/Grammars/SQLiteGrammar.php:450-453 — "Handled on table creation or alteration"), so a `Schema::table()` FK add is applied by `compileAlter()`, which rebuilds the table through `__temp__` (same file:353). The rebuild reconstructs each column from `BlueprintState`, whose `full_type_definition` is the introspected type string (vendor/.../Schema/BlueprintState.php:72) — and SQLite reports an enum column as plain `varchar` because `typeEnum()` emits the constraint as a separate table-level CHECK (SQLiteGrammar.php:873-880). Probe result: before the FK add the DDL was `"role" varchar check ("role" in ('user', 'ai')) not null`; after it was `"role" varchar not null`, and `insert([... 'role' => 'system' ...])` then SUCCEEDED. MySQL keeps a real ENUM (2026_01_01_000090_create_ai_chat_messages_table.php:14, no default, NOT NULL) and rejects it. So phpunit (sqlite :memory:, phpunit.xml) stops enforcing a constraint prod still enforces — the exact trade-off 2026_08_06_000120:17-26 documents and rejects. Any 'memory' work that wants a third role value (system/summary turn) is the case that bites: green in CI, 1265 error in production.

risks.title: The sqlite rebuild copies rows with FK checks disabled, so the FK is never validated in CI — only in prod
risks.detail: `compileAlter()` wraps the `__temp__` copy in `PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF` / `ON` (SQLiteGrammar.php:356-360, gated on the current pragma value). On sqlite the FK therefore passes regardless of dangling session_ids; MySQL's `ALTER TABLE ... ADD FOREIGN KEY` does validate existing rows, so prod is the first place an orphan surfaces — as a failed migration mid-deploy. The existing backfill only covered rows present when ..._000120 ran: `adoptLegacyMessages()` (2026_08_06_000120:78-110) selects `whereNull('session_id')` once, at that migration's up(). Rated high rather than blocker because AiController::query() is the only writer and always sets session_id (AiController.php:211, :240) — but that is a code invariant, not a schema one, and it is unverifiable from the test suite by construction.

risks.title: `seq` is read-then-write with no unique constraint and no transaction — a tie silently deletes turns from the model's memory
risks.detail: AiController.php:204-206 computes `(int) max('seq')` for the session, then inserts at :214 (`++$seq`) and :243 (`++$seq`) with no surrounding `DB::transaction` — contrast destroySession (:138) and clearHistory (:290), which are transactional. The supporting index is `$table->index(['session_id','seq'], ...)` — plain, not unique (2026_08_06_000120:56). Two concurrent POSTs to /ai/query in one session read the same max and write the same seq. `transcript()` then orders `seq DESC, created_at DESC` (AiController.php:503-504) and `created_at` is whole-second DATETIME — which is precisely why seq exists (2026_08_06_000120:28-32) — so the tie resolves arbitrarily. When the reorder puts two same-role turns adjacent, `sanitiseHistory()` pops the OLDER one (app/Services/Ai/AbstractAiProvider.php:174-178) and a trailing user turn is popped at :185-187. Real turns disappear from the replay with no exception and no log entry. This is the failure mode the 'real memory' goal makes consequential, and AiChatSessionTest.php has no concurrency case.

risks.title: A `down()` written the conventional way fails on the sqlite test database
risks.detail: If the FK migration's `down()` drops it by constraint name — `$table->dropForeign('ai_chat_messages_session_id_foreign')` — SQLite throws `RuntimeException('This database driver does not support dropping foreign keys by name.')` (vendor/laravel/framework/src/Illuminate/Database/Schema/Grammars/SQLiteGrammar.php:604-608). Only the column-array form `dropForeign(['session_id'])` compiles (via the same table rebuild). The repo's stated migration convention is that `down()` is a literal inverse (2026_08_16_000001_add_nomination_notes_to_succession_candidates.php:31-36), and every migration is exercised by `RefreshDatabase` on sqlite, so the wrong form is a hard failure the moment anyone rolls back. Related MySQL-side ordering trap: with an FK on the column, 2026_08_06_000120's own `down()` at :64-67 (`dropColumn(['session_id','seq'])`) cannot run until the FK is dropped first.

risks.title: Wiring "New chat" to POST /ai/sessions writes a permanent untitled row that nothing ever collects
risks.detail: `storeSession()` inserts immediately (AiController.php:90-95 → `createSession()` :465-483) with `title => null` and `updated_at => now()`. `sessions()` returns every row unfiltered, ordered `updated_at DESC`, `limit(100)` (:75-79) — no `whereNotNull('title')`, no exists-messages predicate — so an abandoned New chat sits at the top of the history list permanently. The only deletes in the codebase are destroySession (:138-148) and clearHistory (:290-293); there is no cleanup of empty sessions anywhere in app/ or database/seeders/. The current JS deliberately avoids this: startNewChat() nulls the id client-side with a comment saying exactly why (resources/views/layouts/hims.blade.php:866-876, "No POST /ai/sessions here… query() creates it on first send"). The route is nonetheless live (routes/web.php:362) and used by AiChatSessionTest.php:125, so the plan's "New chat button" will find it. With limit(100) and no pagination, accumulated empties also push real conversations out of reach of the list entirely.

risks.title: There is no "last spoken in" column — renaming a conversation reorders the history list
risks.detail: `updateSession()` bumps `updated_at` on a pure rename (AiController.php:117-122), and both list reads sort by it: `sessions()` :77 and `history()` :165 (`orderByDesc('updated_at')`, backed by the ['user_id','updated_at'] index at 2026_08_06_000120:47). `history()` also picks "the most recent conversation" by the same column, so a rename changes which conversation the rail resumes into on next open. `storePending()` bumps it too (:413-417) while `clearPending()` deliberately does not (:420-425), so the column already means several different things. A history list ordered by activity needs a `last_message_at` that only query()'s message insert touches; there is no such column today.

risks.title: Global search over chat history is a leading-wildcard LIKE across the whole message table, per keystroke
risks.detail: `GlobalSearchController::searchAiHistory()` correlates `ai_chat_messages` against each of the user's sessions with `where('chat_message.message', 'like', '%term%')` inside a `whereExists` (lines 814-820), and the outer `limit(self::PER_SOURCE_LIMIT)` is only applied at :825 — after the predicate. `message` is a TEXT column with no FULLTEXT index: 2026_01_01_000090:11-19 creates only the user_id index, and 2026_08_06_000120:56 adds only (session_id, seq). The layout fires this on a 220ms debounce per keystroke (resources/views/layouts/hims.blade.php:462-465). Multiplying sessions per user — the explicit goal of feature (b) — multiplies the correlated scans, and the leading wildcard means no index can ever help.

risks.title: `transcript()` reads ten times the history that can ever be used, on every send
risks.detail: `HISTORY_LIMIT = 200` rows (AiController.php:47, applied at :505) but `capHistory()` keeps only `history_turns` = 20 turns and 12000 chars, discarding the rest from the oldest end (app/Services/Ai/AbstractAiProvider.php:211-227; config/services.php:61-62). `message` is TEXT and replies run to `max_tokens` 1024, so a long conversation pulls a few hundred KB of message bodies out of MySQL per /ai/query request and throws ~90% away before the wire. The same 200-row read also feeds `sessionMessages()` (:98-106), where the full window IS wanted — so the fix is a separate, smaller limit on the replay path, not a change to HISTORY_LIMIT.

risks.title: `query()` is the only chat write path with no transaction — an interrupted request strands a question with no answer
risks.detail: The user-message insert (AiController.php:208-217), the reply insert (:237-248) and the title/updated_at write (:252-254) are three separate statements with no `DB::transaction`, unlike destroySession (:138) and clearHistory (:290). The AI drivers all catch `\Throwable` (GeminiProvider.php:59, OpenAiProvider.php:63, AnthropicProvider.php:63) so `ask()` will not throw, but a PHP `max_execution_time` kill mid-request — plausible given the 30s provider timeout at config/services.php — commits the question and not the reply, leaving `title` null. The transcript then shows an unanswered question while `sanitiseHistory()` pops that trailing user turn out of the replay (AbstractAiProvider.php:185-187), so the screen and the model disagree about what was asked.

risks.lens: Risks of replaying conversation history to the AI provider: token/context blowup on long threads, cost, each provider expecting a DIFFERENT multi-turn body shape, the warning-prefixed never-throw failure contract, ordering/role-mapping bugs, and the fact that CompetencyGapAnalysisService also calls ask() and must NOT get chat history.

risks.title: AI_HISTORY_TURNS=0 — the documented "no memory" kill switch — actually makes history UNLIMITED
risks.detail: config/services.php:54 states "Set AI_HISTORY_TURNS=0 for no memory". AbstractAiProvider.php:213-215 implements the cap as `if (count($turns) > $this->historyTurns()) { $turns = array_slice($turns, -$this->historyTurns()); }`. With historyTurns()=0 the slice is `array_slice($turns, -0)`, and PHP's `-0` is `0`, so it returns the ENTIRE array. Proven by running the real class: 30 stored exchanges (60 turns) in, `history_turns=20` keeps 20, `history_turns=0` keeps all 60. The only setting that actually disables replay is AI_HISTORY_CHARS=0 (verified: keeps 0). This is the one lever an operator has when a thread blows up token cost or when review/patient text must stop leaving the hospital, and setting it does the opposite of what the config comment promises — silently, because nothing fails.

risks.title: The three divergent multi-turn wire shapes have zero test coverage
risks.detail: `grep -rn "Http::fake" tests/` returns nothing, and no test references GeminiProvider, OpenAiProvider, AnthropicProvider or AiManager. Every AI test substitutes a fake implementing `AiProvider` directly (AiChatSessionTest.php:40-59, AiActionTest.php:55, GapAnalysisFeedbackTest.php:159, AiActionPlannerTest.php:48, HimsKnowledgeTest.php:168), so no test ever builds a request body. The only history logic pinned is the shared sanitiser, reached through a hand-rolled subclass at AiChatSessionTest.php:460-480. The three bodies genuinely differ: Gemini emits `contents[]` with roles `user`/`model`, `parts[{text}]`, and NO system field — systemContext is string-concatenated onto the final user turn (GeminiProvider.php:79-99); OpenAI emits `messages[]` with a leading `role:system` message (OpenAiProvider.php:79-93); Anthropic emits `messages[]` plus a separate top-level `system` field, and its buildMessages() takes no $scope at all (AnthropicProvider.php:41-47, 82-96). A role-mapping inversion, a lost turn, or a leading-`ai` turn (which Anthropic rejects outright) in any one driver ships green. The planned change makes replay the headline feature; this is its blind spot.

risks.title: App-authored strings are replayed to the provider as the model's own voice
risks.detail: isSyntheticReply() matches only '⚠️' and AiAccessPolicy::REFUSAL_PREFIX ('🔒', AiAccessPolicy.php:43) — AbstractAiProvider.php:197-201. AiController::query() persists EVERY reply as role 'ai' (AiController.php:237-248), including text no model produced: all AiActionExecutor messages ('Done.' :115, 'Your role does not allow that action.' :52, 'That was rejected: …' :72, 'You are not allowed to do that.' / 'That record could not be found.' :74-76, 'That could not be completed. Nothing was changed.' :80, 'I need that to be clearer — …' :148/:185, 'Tell me which record you mean and I will do it.' :178), AiController's own 'Cancelled — nothing was changed.' (:317) and 'I can do that, but I need … first.' (:339), and each driver's `?? 'No response generated.'` (GeminiProvider.php:48, OpenAiProvider.php:51, AnthropicProvider.php:51). None carries a filtered prefix, so all are replayed as assistant turns. This is exactly the failure AbstractAiProvider.php:113-123 says the filter exists to prevent, and it collides head-on with HimsKnowledge.php:159-161, which instructs the model to "NEVER say you have created, changed or deleted anything unless you were told the action succeeded" — while the transcript teaches it that its own voice says "Done."

risks.title: Every message containing a common English verb costs two full provider round-trips, each carrying the whole 8,500-char system prompt
risks.detail: AiController.php:325-329 runs the ACTION_VERBS pre-filter then calls AiActionPlanner::plan(), which makes its own `ask()` call (AiActionPlanner.php:47). If the planner returns null (AiController.php:331-333) the conversational `ask()` at :234 fires as well — two requests for one message. Both pay the full system block, because every driver unconditionally prepends systemContext() (OpenAiProvider.php:81, AnthropicProvider.php:44, GeminiProvider.php:95); measured at 8,500 chars, of which 8,038 is HimsKnowledge::appGuide() — navigation guidance irrelevant to a JSON classification task. The planner adds the action catalogue on top: measured 7,051 chars for an admin, 756 for staff (AiActionRegistry::catalogueFor). ACTION_VERBS (AiController.php:50-54) matches `add|new|set|change|update|make|log|record|move|mark|open|close` — ordinary words, so a large share of plain questions pay double. No cheaper classifier model exists: the planner receives the same memoised singleton via DI (AiActionPlanner.php:34, AppServiceProvider.php:19-28).

risks.title: The history character budget excludes the system prompt, so the real per-turn ceiling is ~22,200 chars and grows with any budget increase
risks.detail: capHistory() sums only the replayed turns: `array_sum(array_map(fn ($t) => mb_strlen($t['text']), $turns))` (AbstractAiProvider.php:217-223). The system block is never counted, and it is large — measured systemContext(null) = 8,500 chars, +680 for a staff scope fragment = 9,182 (AiAccessPolicy::scopeFor, :188-203). Add the 12,000-char history default (config/services.php:62) and the 1,000-char prompt ceiling (`query` => `max:1000`, AiController.php:186) and one conversational turn sends up to ~22,200 chars ≈ 5,500 input tokens, re-sent in full on every turn of the thread. `max_tokens` = 1024 (config/services.php:59) bounds generation only — AbstractAiProvider.php:88-91 — so it does nothing here. Raising AI_HISTORY_CHARS to "remember more" moves the ceiling linearly with no awareness that ~9,200 chars of fixed text already sits in front of it.

risks.title: A destructive-action exchange is replayed as a bare "confirm" → "Done." with the record it named stripped out
risks.detail: The confirmation prompt is ⚠️-prefixed (AiController.php:366: `"⚠️ {$spec['label']}: **{$prepared['label']}**. This cannot be undone. Reply **confirm** …"`), so isSyntheticReply() drops it AND array_pops the user question that preceded it (AbstractAiProvider.php:162-168). Traced through the real sanitiser: [user "delete user Bob", ai "⚠️ Delete user: **Bob** …", user "confirm", ai "Done."] sanitises to exactly [user "confirm", ai "Done."]. The model is left believing it answered a bare "confirm" with "Done." and has no record of what was deleted, so a follow-up "what did you just remove?" is answered from a transcript with the subject excised. Meanwhile the browser shows the full exchange — loadConversation appends every returned row unfiltered (`data.messages.forEach(m => appendMsg(m.message, m.role))`, layouts/hims.blade.php:899-929) — so screen and model see two different conversations.

risks.title: The '⚠️' discriminator is a bare literal duplicated across 8 files with no shared constant, and four independent copies decide four different things
risks.detail: Its counterpart is a real constant (AiAccessPolicy::REFUSAL_PREFIX, AiAccessPolicy.php:43) but '⚠️' is inlined: 8 occurrences in AbstractAiProvider.php, 3-4 in each driver (GeminiProvider, OpenAiProvider, AnthropicProvider), 2 in NullAiProvider and AiActionPlanner, 1 each in AiController and CompetencyGapAnalysisService. Four separate `str_starts_with(…, '⚠️')` tests key off it for different decisions: drop from replayed history (AbstractAiProvider.php:199), return null from decodeJson (:294), report "AI unavailable" on the gap-analysis screen (CompetencyGapAnalysisService.php:818), and abort action planning (AiActionPlanner.php:86). Reword one driver's failure string, add a provider that prefixes differently, or lose the variation selector (U+FE0F — `str_starts_with` is byte-exact) and history sanitising silently stops filtering while the gap-analysis page starts trying to JSON-decode an error message. Nothing fails; a warning just becomes model voice.

risks.title: seq is assigned by an unguarded read-then-write, so two concurrent sends in one session produce duplicate seq and nondeterministic replay order
risks.detail: AiController.php:204-206 reads `max('seq')` for the session, then :208 and :237 insert `++$seq` — no DB::transaction, no row lock, and the covering index is a plain one, not unique (`$table->index(['session_id','seq'], 'ai_chat_messages_session_seq_index')`, migration 2026_08_06_000120:56). Two in-flight requests both read the same max and write the same pair of seq values. Reachable two ways: the Enter handler calls sendQuery() with no in-flight guard (layouts/hims.blade.php:996-998) — `sendBtn.disabled = true` at :948 blocks only the button, and the provider timeout is 30s (config/services.php:60), a wide window; and `hims_ai_session` lives in localStorage (layouts/hims.blade.php:621-625, :980), which is shared across tabs, so two tabs are on the SAME session by design with no cross-tab coordination. Once seq ties, transcript()'s `orderByDesc('seq')->orderByDesc('created_at')` (AiController.php:503-504) falls back to a whole-second timestamp — the exact tie the seq column was added to fix (migration 2026_08_06_000120:28-32) — and sanitiseHistory then "repairs" the scrambled order by silently deleting turns.

risks.title: Legacy adopted messages have no deterministic order and are mispaired on replay, attaching one question to another question's answer
risks.detail: adoptLegacyMessages() moves every pre-existing message into an "Earlier conversation" session but deliberately leaves seq NULL: "seq is left null for adopted rows — created_at is the only ordering information that exists for them" (migration 2026_08_06_000120:102-104). The same file's docblock explains why that is not enough: "AiController wrote one now() value to both the question and the answer row, and the column has whole-second precision, so the two halves of a turn tie… the replayed turn list sent to the model must be in the true order" (:28-32). The fix was never applied to the rows it describes. So intra-pair order for that session is whatever the engine returns, and when a pair comes back answer-first sanitiseHistory's alternation forcing mispairs rather than reorders: run through the real class, [A1, Q1, A2, Q2] yields exactly [user "Q1", ai "A2 answers Q2"] — Q1 credited with Q2's answer, A1 and Q2 discarded. The session is listed in the sidebar and selectable, so this replays on any real deployment carrying pre-migration history.

risks.title: Gemini — the default provider — puts the 8,500-char system block LAST, behind the variable history, so the request has no stable prefix
risks.detail: GeminiProvider.php:93-96 appends the system prompt to the final user turn (`'parts' => [['text' => $this->systemContext($scope)."\n\nUser question: ".$prompt]]`) because system_instruction is unsupported on older models. OpenAI and Anthropic put the identical block first, where it is a fixed leading prefix (OpenAiProvider.php:81; AnthropicProvider.php:44 as a top-level `system` field). Today, with no replay, the guide is effectively the whole Gemini request. Once 20 turns of history are prepended, ~8,500 chars of unchanging text sits behind ~12,000 chars of text that changes every turn, so it can never form a stable request prefix on the one provider that is the configured default (config/services.php:57, and CLAUDE.md's services rule states Gemini is the default so the existing key keeps working). The same replay change therefore has materially different request economics per provider, and the cheapest-to-cache arrangement is the one the default provider structurally cannot use.

risks.title: AI_HISTORY_TURNS and AI_HISTORY_CHARS are absent from .env.example
risks.detail: .env.example documents the neighbouring AI knobs — AI_PROVIDER at :116, AI_TEMPERATURE :117, AI_MAX_TOKENS :118, AI_TIMEOUT :119, then per-provider keys and models :122-137 — but neither history variable appears anywhere in the file. They are read only at config/services.php:61-62. So the two settings that bound request size, per-turn cost, and how much of a conversation leaves the hospital for a third party are invisible to whoever configures the box; the pathway to discovering them is reading config/services.php. Combined with the inverted AI_HISTORY_TURNS=0 behaviour above, an operator who does find the comment and follows it gets unlimited replay.

risks.title: The "gap analysis must not receive chat history" invariant holds today but nothing pins it
risks.detail: CompetencyGapAnalysisService calls `$this->ai->ask($prompt)` with no second argument at :648 and :691, so $history defaults to [] (AiProvider.php:51); AiActionPlanner.php:47 does the same. Drivers hold no state, and AiProvider.php:17-22 documents why (memoised singletons shared by every consumer, so a driver remembering turns would leak one user's chat into another request and into the gap analysis). Correct as built. But GapAnalysisFeedbackTest's spy accepts `array $history = []` in its signature and records only `$prompt` (:159-165) — no assertion that $history arrived empty — and no test exercises AiActionPlanner's call site for the same property. Contrast AiChatSessionTest, which does assert `$spy->seenHistory` three times (:102, :111, :132). So the chat side is pinned and the two must-stay-clean callers are not: an edit that threads history through a shared helper, or a driver that starts caching turns, ships green.

risks.title: An unknown or garbled storage role defaults to ASSISTANT, not user
risks.detail: `$role = ($entry['role'] ?? '') === 'user' ? 'user' : 'ai';` (AbstractAiProvider.php:150). Anything that is not exactly the string 'user' — a missing key, a truncated value, a future third role — becomes an assistant turn, i.e. text the model is told it said. The safe default runs the other way: an unattributable row should be read as user input, never as model voice. This is not purely hypothetical on the test connection: migration 2026_08_06_000120:17-26 warns that a Schema::table() FK would rebuild the SQLite table and silently downgrade the `role` enum('user','ai') CHECK constraint to a plain varchar, leaving MySQL with a real ENUM and sqlite with no constraint at all — so the one connection the suite runs on is the one with nothing enforcing the two legal values.

risks.title: 200 message rows are read and mapped on every /ai/query to feed a 20-turn cap
risks.detail: transcript() fetches `limit(self::HISTORY_LIMIT)` = 200 rows with their full `message` text, maps and reverses them (AiController.php:498-513, constant at :48), and query() calls it on every single send (:202). sanitiseHistory then keeps at most historyTurns() = 20 (AbstractAiProvider.php:213, default at config/services.php:61), so ~180 rows of chat text are pulled out of MySQL and discarded per message. The two limits are set in different files with no relationship between them, so tuning AI_HISTORY_TURNS down does not reduce the read, and raising it above 200 silently caps at the controller's constant instead.
